text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm rejects the idea of an exchange rate policy for the euro. (p1)
- Health minister Els Borst says she will push for higher healthcare budget. (p1)
- SHV Holdings is in talks with Swiss/German group Metro on the sale of its Makro bulk retail stores. (p3)
- Alitalia says it is talking to KLM about a possible alliance. (p3)
- Publishers ask economic affairs minister Hans Wijers to end unfair competition in the media market. (p4)
- Pay-TV firm Canal Plus pays 145 million guilders for rights to broadcast Dutch premier league soccer matches. (p1)
- Retailers' turnover in May is 6.3 pct higher than in same period of last year. (p2)
- Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm sceptical about the soundness of Italy's bugdet. (p2)
- Dutch banks plan to present new system to combat fraud. (p1)
- Lovers Rail, recently taken over by France's CGEA, now plans to enter the bus segment of the public transport market. (p7)
- Environment Minister Margaretha de Boer reaches agreement with businesses on limiting waste from packaging material. (p19)
- There is a growing difference in the level of health between rich and poor in the Netherlands. (p1)
- Leiden-based biotech firm Pharming says it holds the rights to artificial blood plasma currently claimed by Scottish rival PPL Therapeutics. (p5)
